transcription_note: TRANSCRIBED FROM THE PAGE IMAGES, NOT FROM THE PDF TEXT LAYER. The earlier artefact in this session (08263082ebdda8eb.json) was made from pypdf's text layer, which is badly damaged, and recorded that damage as though it were a property of the DOCUMENT -- authors 'illegible', years 'not resolvable', one title's slope term 'NOT legible'. The pages are JBIG2 images and render legibly in about a second. Every such claim in the earlier artefact is withdrawn. The per-entry `note` fields below record what the first pass got wrong, so the correction is auditable rather than silent.
completeness: 38 entries, ANSI to Webb, strict alphabetical order with no break, ending at the GPO imprint on page index 169. Read off the rendered pages.

reference.unstructured: Templer, J.A. Stair shape and human movement, Unpublished doctoral dissertation. New York: Columbia University, 1974.
reference.note: COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY, printed plainly; the first pass wrote '[?] [Un]iversity'. THE ENTRY IS STILL 1974 AND STILL ABOUT STAIRS, so the discrepancy with Table 13 footnote c's 'Templer, 1977' is real. BUT THE CONCLUSION BATCH 19 DREW FROM IT WAS FALSE: adversarial review found Templer, J.A., Provisions for elderly and handicapped pedestrians, FHWA-RD-79-1/-2/-3, Georgia Tech Pedestrian Research Laboratory -- whose Volume 3 contains 'A Study of Short Ramps', 32 gradient-rating tables for manual and electric wheelchair users, and Table 20 'Ramp Gradient Recommendations' over 1:8, 1:10, 1:12 and 1:16. Templer has substantial ramp research; this bibliography simply cites a different item of his.
